text:
## Observations

1. A single building always qualifies, and every selection of two or more buildings has a common index gap from 1 to N − 1.
2. For a fixed gap, the longest valid selection ending at a building extends the longest selection ending one gap earlier if that building exists and has the same height. Otherwise, the longest selection ending there has length one.
3. Scanning from front to back computes each predecessor’s length before it is needed. Each gap can be processed independently using the same length array.

## Solution sketch

> A single building always qualifies, and every selection of two or more buildings has a common index gap from 1 to N − 1.

1. Read N and the heights. Initialize the answer to one, then process each gap from 1 to N − 1. If N is one, there are no gaps to process and the answer is one.

> For a fixed gap, the longest valid selection ending at a building extends the longest selection ending one gap earlier if that building exists and has the same height. Otherwise, the longest selection ending there has length one.

2. For each gap, scan the buildings from front to back. If the building one gap earlier exists and has the same height, store its length plus one for the current building. Otherwise, store one. Update the answer with each stored length. Every valid selection of two or more buildings has a gap and an ending position examined by this scan. If all heights are distinct, every stored length is one.

> Scanning from front to back computes each predecessor’s length before it is needed. Each gap can be processed independently using the same length array.

3. Reuse one length array across all gap scans. Whenever a length is read, its entry has already been overwritten for the current gap. Print the answer after the scans. There are N − 1 scans of N buildings with constant work per building, so the algorithm takes O(N²) time and O(N) space.

isolation.mechanism: codex exec, fresh ephemeral session, empty temporary working directory, user config and exec rules ignored, read-only sandbox, web search and listed features disabled, credential-like variables removed from the environment
isolation.limits: Codex harness instructions and its own tool descriptions remain in the model context; they cannot be removed. Tool isolation is verified post hoc from the event stream, which contained no tool, command, file or search events.
